title: CodeStatement & Metric Identity vs. Display Label
subtitle: Domain model review: separating canonical slug identity, canonical human label, and authored user text across parser, editor, and runtime.

components.title: The Three Faces of an Effort Reference
components.body: Every workout statement that references an effort, equipment item, or tag deals with three distinct strings: (1) the user's authored text or alias in the script (e.g. 'KB Swings'), (2) the canonical human-friendly display label ('Kettlebell Swing'), and (3) the durable system slug ('kettlebell-swing') used for timing, MET enrichment, and WQL indexing. Today, IMetric and ICodeStatement collapse these three concepts into two overloaded fields (value and image) plus an optional sidecar metadata bag, causing slugs to leak into editor completions, raw JSON suffixes, and runtime labels.

components.title: The 3 distinct representations a statement must carry
components.body: A single movement token on a workout line serves three different consumers that each require a different representation.
rows: Overwritten when explicit JSON or autocomplete inserts a raw slug like 'dumbbell-snatch'.
Autocomplete insertion, Timer Stack display, Review Grid, Insight Pill
IMetric.name is unused on EffortMetric; LabelComposer & computeLabel() read metric.image instead of canonical label.
EffortMetric.value (when resolved) or raw authored text (when unresolved)

components.title: Where the Current Domain Model Falls Short
components.body: Inspecting packages/core and packages/lang reveals four structural gaps in how ICodeStatement and IMetric model identity versus display.

items.title: Overloaded value & image, missing label
items.body: In EffortMetric (packages/lang/src/runtime/compiler/metrics/EffortMetric.ts), this.value = options?.resolvedSlug ?? effort and this.image = effort. It never populates IMetric.name (the canonical human label), and when parsed without a ReferenceIndex, value is the raw text rather than a slug.

items.title: Split equipment + effort shares raw source text
items.body: When '10 Dumbbell Snatch' resolves via split matching (equipment: 'dumbbell', effort: 'snatch'), EffortMetric.image is still set to 'Dumbbell Snatch' and EquipmentMetric.image is ALSO set to 'Dumbbell Snatch'. Any consumer reading metric.image duplicates the phrase.

items.title: Dead exerciseId field on ICodeStatement
items.body: ICodeStatement (packages/core/src/models/CodeStatement.ts) declares exerciseId?: string, and BlockTemplateComposer passes anchorStatement.exerciseId to BlockContext. Yet semantic-classifier.ts never sets statement.exerciseId—leaving runtime blocks without direct statement-level effort identity.

items.title: Runtime re-resolves from block.label string
items.body: Because ICodeStatement does not expose structured resolved references at the statement level, EffortEnrichmentPass (line 93) reads block.label (a formatted display string built by LabelComposer) and runs references.resolve(block.label) all over again at runtime.

components.title: How This Domain Gap Breaks the Editor & UI
components.body: Because the domain model treats slug as the primary value and hides the human-friendly name inside an optional metadata array, the UI layer is forced into awkward compromises.

components.title: Concrete UI symptoms in ```time blocks
items: Autocomplete inserts slugs instead of human names: In NoteEditor.tsx, NOTE_NESTED_WQL_OPTIONS maps efforts to { value: effort.slug, label: `${effort.label} (${effort.slug})` }. Selecting 'Back Squat (back-squat)' in a ```time block inserts the hyphenated slug 'back-squat' into the workout text, which looks like machine code and can even fail Lezer's bare Identifier grammar rule.

Explicit reference overrides leak raw JSON into workout lines: When a user picks an effort or equipment from the line picker, buildLineWithRefs() appends {"effort":"burpee","equipment":["kettlebell"]} to the end of the line because there is no clean syntax or statement binding that keeps the friendly name in the text while binding the slug.

Double chips in the inline metric panel: MetricInlinePanel iterates over statement.metrics (rendering an 'Exercise: Dumbbell Snatch' chip from EffortMetric.image) AND iterates over metadata.references.refs (rendering 'Snatch' and 'Dumbbell' chips), showing redundant and conflicting names for the same words.

Split-phrase highlighting overlap: On 'KB Swings', EquipmentMetric and EffortMetric both record startOffset at 'KB', so the equipment underline and effort underline paint on top of each other unless the UI manually slices character offsets.

Timer & Review labels ignore canonical names: LabelComposer.ts and labelFormatting.ts (baseText) read metric.image first. If a line was authored with a shorthand alias or explicit JSON, the runtime timer and review table cannot choose between the user's alias and the canonical effort label.

components.title: Proposed Domain Model Architecture
components.body: Fix the root cause in @bitcobblers/wod-wiki-core and @bitcobblers/wod-wiki-lang by making the three-part identity (slug, canonical label, authored text) first-class on both IMetric and ICodeStatement.

components.title: 1. First-class fields on EffortMetric, EquipmentMetric, and ICodeStatement
components.body: Promote display label and matched alias/token out of untyped metadata bags onto the typed model.
rows:
value: slug | rawText
image: rawFullPhrase
name: undefined

value: slug (or undefined if unresolved)
name: canonicalLabel (e.g. 'Kettlebell Swing')
image: matchedTokenText (e.g. 'Swings')
Timing/analytics always read metric.value for the slug; UI badges read metric.name for canonical label or metric.image for exact matched text.

value: string[] (slugs)
name: canonicalLabels.join(', ')
image: matchedPrefixText (e.g. 'KB')
Separates the equipment prefix token ('KB') from the movement token ('Swings') in both text and character offsets.
{ kind, slug, label, authored, matchedAlias?, span?: { from, to } }
Records which alias or label was matched and its exact slice within the statement.

exerciseId?: string (populated with effortRef.slug)
references?: StatementReferences
Gives the JIT compiler and EffortEnrichmentPass direct O(1) access to resolved effort/equipment slugs and labels without re-parsing block.label.

items.title: Run reference resolution after unit fusion
items.body: In lezer-mapper.ts, run reference resolution after dialectStack.processAll() (unit fusion) so residual efforts like '20m Row' -> 'Row' resolve their slug and canonical label cleanly, and split phrases ('KB Swings') assign non-overlapping SyntaxMeta ranges to Equipment ('KB') and Effort ('Swings').

items.title: Surface-aware label composition
items.body: Update LabelComposer and MetricPresentationPolicy.computeLabel() to support a display preference: 'authored' (keeps user alias in editor context) vs 'canonical' (shows 'Kettlebell Swing' on Timer Stack and Analytics tables using metric.name).

items.title: Read slug directly from statement / metric
items.body: In EffortEnrichmentPass, read the canonical effort slug directly from the block's EffortMetric.value (or statement.exerciseId) instead of re-running string resolution on block.label. The timer display can show the friendly name while the engine keys off the slug.

components.title: Proposed Editor & UI Layer Experience
components.body: With the domain model carrying both the slug and the human-friendly label/alias, the editor inside ```time blocks becomes clean, obvious, and non-invasive on both desktop and mobile.

items.title: Display & insert friendly names, resolve to slugs
items.body: When typing in a ```time block, autocomplete shows 'Back Squat' (with 'back-squat' as subtle detail badge) and inserts 'Back Squat'—never the raw hyphenated slug. Only explicit property lines (effort: "back-squat") insert slugs. If a user selects via a known alias ('KB Swing'), the editor can keep their alias in text while the resolver binds the slug.

items.title: Show canonical identity without duplicating tokens
items.body: Because the line itself already says '10 KB Swings @24kg', the end-of-line insight pill doesn't repeat 'Exercise: KB Swings'. Instead, it shows the resolved canonical mapping: [⏱ 10] [🧰 Kettlebell ↗] [🏋 Kettlebell Swing ↗] [⚖ 24kg]—proving to the author that their shorthand resolved to the right system entities.

items.title: Turn unknown text into an Effort, Alias, or Equipment
items.body: When a line contains an unknown token (e.g. '10 Zercher Carry #heavy-day'), it gets a subtle dashed amber underline and a compact '? Zercher Carry · Define ▾' pill. Tapping it offers one-tap inline actions: '+ Effort' (creates slug 'zercher-carry' with label 'Zercher Carry'), '+ Alias' (links 'Zercher Carry' as an alias to an existing effort slug via palette), '+ Equipment', or '+ Tag'.

items.title: Zero layout shift, responsive wrapping
items.body: No inter-row spacer widgets are injected into CodeMirror, so arrowing up/down never shifts lines vertically. On desktop, the insight pill sits inline at the end of the active row; on mobile (375px) or long lines, it docks as a compact floating pill below the active line and hides automatically whenever the autocomplete dropdown is open.

components.title: Recommended Implementation Sequence
components.body: Ordered from core domain contract outward to editor extensions.

items.title: Enrich ReferenceRef & ICodeStatement
items.body: Add matchedAlias / authored span to ReferenceRef and populate statement.exerciseId + statement-level reference summary.

items.title: Separate value (slug), name (canonical label), and image (authored text) on EffortMetric & EquipmentMetric
items.body: Assign distinct SyntaxMeta ranges on split equipment+effort phrases, run post-fusion reference resolution, and update EffortEnrichmentPass to read slug identity directly.

items.title: Insert human-friendly labels in WhiteboardScript autocomplete
items.body: Update whiteboardScriptCompletionSource and NoteEditor's nested options so bare effort/equipment slots insert the display label (or alias) while property slots insert slugs.

items.title: Unify token underlining, end-of-line insight pill, and inline creation
items.body: Remove inter-row block spacers, deduplicate metric/reference chips in MetricInlinePanel, hide panel during active autocomplete, and wire one-tap Effort / Alias / Equipment / Tag creation.
